So your statement reflects you saying that your detachment commander met Lukic in Pristina [Realtime transcript read in error "Prizren"] and that you knew this from your deputy company commander. Now, why did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Tell us now what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this was understood wrongly. I said that my commander used to go to meetings in Prizren, and on one occasion I drove the deputy company commander to that meeting. That's all in that context. I didn't mention Pristina. It was probably misunderstood and wrongly written down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The trouble with that is that you subsequently signed it, which tends to acknowledge that it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only said what I saw and what I knew. Maybe I failed to notice that that's what it said, but I'm sure I didn't say this. I know about the meetings in Prizren, not about meetings in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one clarification. It might add up to the confusion. Page 53, line 7. Your question was in "Pristina" and in transcript it says "Prizren."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. It should be Pristina. Mr. Marcussen, you were going to say something I think?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If the Court would allow me to, I think I would like to proceed with the rest of the examination and consider whether I need to get back on this point. There are some other issues that I need to consider in this regard. So if you would allow me to leave this one hanging in the air or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. You will have to address us on how you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- intend to tackle it, because all I've done is establish for the moment whether the witness, at this stage, accepts the accuracy of the statement, which he doesn't. But it's a separate question for you to decide whether you wish to pursue to establish whether this is in fact a statement he gave or not, and that's the matter that will be left in abeyance until -- and indeed any other questions in relation to this issue until you decide what you wish to do. It's now an appropriate time for us to have the break in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We need to have your break again. This time it will be for 20 minutes. We'll presume at -- well, we will resume at 25 minutes past, for the avoidance of any doubt. We will go into closed session while you leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K79, during the operations in September 1998, did you go to the Bajgora area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when in September that was, what part of September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly, but I think it was around mid-September, around the 10th or 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where in that area did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Above the Stari Trg mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe what happened when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a house, we found three Albanians and two women.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. We would just object. The same line of objections, that this is not part of our indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But this is the part that you say is in the pre-trial brief; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but not specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just reference to Bajgora as an area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We note the objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back just a little bit. How did you get to Bajgora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On trucks up to the mine of Stari Trg, and then we went up to the hill on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you came to the hill, what instructions were you given there in relation to the operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were supposed to clean up the area from members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you search houses in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were there any -- any people in the houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In some there were, and in others there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you find any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where the three men and the two women were we found a rifle and a combat vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were shot dead, executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Without mentioning any names, could you tell us who shot the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The policemen who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How far away were you from the place where the men were shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fifty metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were these police part of your detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see the people getting shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Before they got shot, did anything happen to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they questioned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how were they treated during the questioning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see what part of the body the men were shot in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where were they shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and what happened to the two women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was an elderly one and the other one was younger. I think the younger one was raped, and afterwards they were both shot dead, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see them getting raped, or did you see the young one get raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw through the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you see them getting killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where were you when you saw that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Still looking through the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them out, and they killed them outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What happened to -- to the house where this -- did anything happen to the house where these things had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house was set on fire later when we started leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm moving on to something else, but I think we need to go into private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we do that, are you able to name any of the police officers involved in this -- rather, the policemen involved in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K79, after the incident that we have just been talking about, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to the inner area of Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you stay there overnight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe that house for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's an older house. That was the only house in that area. A woman lived there and a young man who was mentally ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour. It's before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's noted, Mr. Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you spend the night at the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anyone from your -- from your company do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The command squad spent the night in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anything happen to the woman and the young man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were killed in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know who killed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I think I'll ask that we go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you went back to the base. How did you get back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On trucks, the same way -- the same way we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Approximately, where did you get back on the trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were walking and the trucks were waiting for us somewhere, I think, around Vucitrn or in front of it. Or was it Obilic? I can't remember. And then we boarded the trucks and we went to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How many vehicles were you in when you were driving back to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were seven or eight trucks; two or three jeeps; two tanks, I think; and two Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: As you were driving back, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We met up with another unit in Pristina; and then from Pristina to Suva Reka, as we were taking that road, we were overtaken by car. I think it was a Toyota Corolla or something like that; then the car was stopped. there were two young men in the car. They were taken out, beaten up and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the same objection for the record as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you -- did you see them getting killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All of that happened behind our truck, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was your detachment commander in the column of cars that were driving back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was, but he was in front, at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did he know that these people were getting killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In September, during these operations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move off this. How did the car come to be stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Jeep that was behind us blocked the road for that vehicle, and then that vehicle had to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not following. You originally said that you were overtaken by this car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not my truck. The convoy that was behind us was being overtaken by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: During the operations in -- in September, did you come across groups of refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All over: Drenica, Cicavica, Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And in your estimate, how big were these groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did you ever get close to any of these groups of refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did any of your members of your detachment ever make close contact with some of these refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All of us were in close contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were -- were there any ever -- were there ever any incidents that you witnessed where refugees were asked to hand over money or other valuables?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's noted, Mr. Lukic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they went from one refugee to another and asked for money, or they'd call one representative from each group and ask for money, and they told them if they didn't give any money they would kill all of them. That was done by a small group of policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and these policemen, that small group of policemen, were they from your detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- were women also asked to hand over money or valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody. It was women who had the money on them for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they ever searched, or were they just asked for money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In some cases, there were searches; but in most cases, they asked for money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you ever witness any women being asked to take their clothes off so they could be checked that they were not hiding money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They asked one of them to take off her bra because that's usually where they kept their money.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could avoid leading questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what -- what -- what unit the people who took the money belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did they keep the money for themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were any of the officers in your detachment ever given any money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They shared it with the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did you see that yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. My platoon commander protested against that, but nothing came out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you ever witness anything that could be described as looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was an eyewitness of what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we go on to anything else, let's clarify your platoon commander's position. You said, "he protested." I take it that he wasn't protesting that he wasn't getting his share, so tell us what his protest was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He protested because they were taking money from the refugees in that way. He even wanted to have a fight with the company commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And to whom did he make the protest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the company commander. He told him it was not in order, that this was looting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you ever witness your company commander sharing any other things other than money and jewellery with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He brought three truckloads of technical goods, TV sets, video recorders, video cameras, washing machines. And this is all common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see these trucks yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did all this -- all these things, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These things were from the houses in the various villages. It was taken and loaded onto trucks. A group of five or six men did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did you see those three trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In our base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: During these operations, were you also in the area of the village of Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Glogovac is not a village, it's a town; but yes, yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anybody from your detachment kill anyone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see that killing yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Please describe what it was you saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just the same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A policeman killed two civilians. He ordered them to lie down and then he shot them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we should go into private session and deal with some different matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When -- when the NATO bombing started on the 24th of March, 1999, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So that would be in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And were you sent out on -- on an operation on that day or shortly after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 25th in the morning, we went in the direction of the village of Velika Hoca, Zociste, Opterusa, Dobrodeljani, and then Pagarusa to mop up that area of KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you say "we." Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm referring to my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you have -- have any support by tanks and Pragas on this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but only as far as Opterusa. They did not fire on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see any refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you stay in the evening of the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the hills around those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was anybody killed that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What about the next morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two civilians were killed in Drobodeljani and one civilian in Pagarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... out of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we're now in 1999. Can you help me where this is covered in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is not a specifically charged incident. It is in the Orahovac-Suva Reka area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why don't we concentrate the evidence in this case on what we've got charges for?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Because in our submission, this is relevant to the nature of the operation that was carried out. Now, we have shown how operations were carried out in July, from July through to the end of the year of 1998. We have shown how there have been evidence also from other witnesses in both what we call crime base and internationals about all these operations with a view to establish what happened with these operations. It's part of our case that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What operations -- what evidence from internationals about all the operations are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, all the different reports that have been from the OSCE, the KVM, concerns about the way the heavy handedness of the operations, allegations that crimes were being committed during these so-called anti-terrorist operations. Now, this is -- this witness have given evidence about confirming that actually crimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, give me an example of what you're referring to about reports establishing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't have the specific exhibit numbers. Maybe I should have had that. But a witness like Drewienkiewicz was here and told about how they continuously would raise concerns about the way these anti-terrorist operations were carried out. We've had a number of other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But he wasn't telling us about -- he wasn't giving evidence about people witnessing atrocities directly. It wasn't evidence of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Because the KVM reporters were not there on the ground to see themselves. What we have here is a witness who was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why don't you just include in the indictment on such-and-such a day this witness was in X, or just make the averment that people were killed in the course of an operation. Is it in the pre-trial brief this stuff?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: As -- as part of the general operations that were carried out in Kosovo from -- I mean, we're now within the indictment period -- a specifically charged incident. We're talking about an event which took place at the same time as the crime at Suva Reka and all the other locations that we -- most of the locations, the events that took place right after the NATO bombing started. Now, part of this case is about whether or not that was a part of a wide-spread or systematic attack. Now, it might be sufficient for the Chamber to make inferences just from the specifically charged incidents. The Prosecution would like to lead further evidence about how these -- these operations were carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How is it you decide which ones to charge and which ones not to charge?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There is a limit to how much I can go into this. But, Your Honour, we have -- as I said earlier, this is a witness who stepped forward quite late in the process. He was selected because he was an insider who would be willing to come and tell about this. We think it's important that we hear people from the Serb side who step forward and talk about these events. We would have had to amend the indictment in June or something like that to include the specifics if we had been wanting to charge these different incidents as charged incidents with which -- where we're questioning -- that we want to hold the accused responsible, or even if we just wanted to add the facts as background facts. At that point in time, it was considered too late in the day for something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: To late to put it in the indictment, but not too late to lead it as part of your case. I mean, that doesn't make any logical sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, in our submission, it's covered by the general allegations in the indictment and for -- it is sufficient to give -- to disclose these statements to the Defence so they can prepare their -- they've been having more than half a year to prepare for this witness to come and testify. There are also practical considerations that have gone into this. We've been trying to accommodate a trial schedule after the indictment had been amended -- well, actually four times. One was a third amended indictment. So all these factors lead to the Prosecutor exercising her discretion the way she has. If -- in an ideal world, we would have been able to carry out a full investigation, finish the investigation, make a final indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've had eight years to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. But yet we still had a witness like this step forward in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But there has to be some finality to things that happen in the world. We have to move on. It's a constantly advancing world and there must be a limit drawn somewhere on the way in which the trial process is to be conducted. Let's consider the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will follow the same course with this as we have been following, but we should indicate we are less sympathetic at the moment to this particular situation. The fact that additional witnesses come forward is not in itself justification for just piling them into the case, when clearly this indictment was drawn the Prosecution believed they had a case to present. It doesn't follow that it's legitimate to lead witnesses speaking about incidents that are not in the indictment just because they happen to come forward late. But we will review this question along with the other objections at the end of the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think we need to go in-- very briefly to private session once again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The day after this occurred, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to Korisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where -- where did you stay -- sorry. When did you come to Korisa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around the 2nd or 3rd of April, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's noted, Mr. Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where were you before you came to Korisa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were in that area. I already said Opterusa, Pagarusa, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And while you were there around the -- the 2nd of April, did you witness any more people getting killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there before the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. Where were you before the 2nd of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pagarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what happened at Pagarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An old man was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was he killed by a member of your detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We'll get back to this, but I'll move on to something else. So after this occurred, you were in Korisa.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was -- was your company commander there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did your detachment commander also come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How was the morale in your -- in your company at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think it was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did you hear a conversation between your company commander and the detachment commander about the morale in your unit -- in your company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you heard, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The detachment commander said to our commander to let the army loot so that morale would be higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the translation, this came across as he said that the -- he should let the army loot. Was that what he said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He meant us. He meant policemen, but that was the word he used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and after that, what were you -- were you ordered to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were ordered to move Albanians out of a village there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljubizda.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's necessary to object again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, you should, and I note the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What were you ordered to -- was any force used to achieve this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No force. We went from one house to the other and told the Albanians that they had to move out, to go towards Prizren. We were driving them out and the army was bringing them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they told to leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Why did the army bring them back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in -- in the village Ljubizda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see any refugees in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Refugees were all over the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell me how long they were away from their homes in Ljubizda before the army brought them back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps about two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And did that happen only once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. At that moment, as we were driving them out, the army was bringing them back into the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity the villagers were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were some Serbs, some Albanians, and some Gorani. So the composition of the village was mixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your original answer was that you were ordered to move Albanians out of Ljubizda, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you didn't have to move the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, the -- do you know what the ethnicity of the villagers that -- that returned to the village were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Albanians and Gorani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have an awful lot more to do, but I do maybe have another 15 minutes or 20 minutes or something like that. So I see we are approaching the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can take another five minutes just now and then we'll finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Around this time, were you at the it Suva Reka-Prizren road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the road that goes by Korisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see refugees on that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they sort of in one -- could you describe how that looked? How -- what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a long column on the road. There were vehicles, tractors, trucks full of people, and they were all moving towards Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How long was the column, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly but it was long, I think, about 30 kilometres. My colleagues talked about it, and they said it was about 30 kilometres, almost from Suva Reka to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're in a rather different territory are we not, Mr. Lukic, when we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we're not, Your Honour. Time frame, completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There's a general allegation in the indictment that 800.000 Albanians were expelled from Kosovo from March until July 1999. And these events, we've heard plenty of crime base witnesses talking about being expelled from the Suva Reka area and other parts of Kosovo from March, in April, and May. This -- I'm going to clarify with the witness when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know offhand if we've had evidence relating to April or May, because the averments relate to March.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, definitely, it's not in the pre-trial brief or in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll reserve this question also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When did you -- when did you see this column? About what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd and 3rd of April, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where were you on -- on the 5th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 5th of April, we were in the village of Budakovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this going to be a suitable point to interrupt, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That objection is also noted and will be taken along with the others. That brings the proceedings for today to an end, K79. You'll need to return tomorrow. That will be at 9.00. We will continue your evidence at that stage. It's very important that between now and then you do not discuss your evidence with anyone, and by that I mean anyone at all, and that refers either to the evidence you've given or the evidence you may yet give. You can talk about anything else to anybody you want, but not about the evidence to anyone. Now, we'll go into closed session so that you can leave the courtroom. Can we have the button at that end as well, please, from the security officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of February, 2007, at 9:00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.53 p.m.,
